key_insight: FL4N represents a changing 3D scene in a unified latent space rather than with explicit 4D primitives. The paper presents it as the first feed-forward latent model for rendering dynamic scenes from new viewpoints and timestamps.
problem_solved: Reconstructing dynamic scenes from monocular input requires understanding both 3D structure and motion over time. Existing feed-forward approaches based on explicit 4D Gaussians can produce temporal inconsistencies and severe rendering artifacts.
method: Use a feed-forward model for 4D novel view synthesis.
Encode a 4D scene prior into a unified latent representation instead of explicit 4D primitives.
Use this representation to support rendering across viewpoints and timestamps; further architectural details are not available in the truncated abstract.
impact: FL4N introduces a latent alternative to explicit Gaussian-based dynamic scene representations. It could help practitioners develop more temporally coherent rendering systems, though the provided excerpt includes no quantitative results.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: monocular input → feed-forward model → unified latent scene → novel-view frames.

paper_title: FL4N: Feed-forward Latent Model for 4D Novel View Synthesis
paper_authors: Eunbeen Hong, Hyeonseo Yu, Honggyu An, Jooho Son, Hyunah Ko
